A and B, Enterprise Integration Patterns, Patterns of Enterprise Application
Architecture, RxJS core, RxJS practice, GEB map parts 1 and 2, Team Topologies
map parts 1 to 3) is classified once into the app's own catalog as a tool a
unit can be given, a scene element, a metric or a background concept; every
tool carries the five faces (scene, selection, transform, observable, toy
metric), a transform from the closed enum or `untyped` with its reason, and
an analog only when obvious; the catalog is committed as the app's own data

generic terms and refuses every other map field; the per-work scene type and
the first three tools per work are recorded; and the operator browses and
filters the catalog at `/tools/catalog`.

orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens Tools, Catalog
and sees the six works as a shelf, each with its title, its row count and the
scene it feeds. They choose AI for Games and see its chapters as a table of
contents with a concept count per chapter; they open Chapter 3 Movement and
see its sections and their concepts; they choose Two-level formation
steering and read, in a measure set for reading, its definition in full, its
type, its place in the book (part, chapter, section, subsection), its related
concepts as links in running text (Anchor point, Slot, Fixed formations), the
hook the map's author suggested for DotLn as a sentence, and, because the
tool is typed, its five faces rendered as one sentence (give it to a
formation of three or more units on terrain; it steers an anchor as a
character and the members to slots; watch the anchor-to-mean distance and
the slot error; measure the assignment cost) with its parameters and their
defaults. They follow Slot to its own reading and return. They type "arrive"
into the search and reach Arrive in two keystrokes and one click. On Arrive
they read that the soldier scene runs it, and once the scene exists a link
opens the scene with that tool chosen. Their last ten readings persist
across a reload. A concept whose definition the run marked as the mapping
worker's own reading says so beside the definition. Nothing on the page is a
label-value list with nothing to read. What the operator learns is what each
concept is and how a work hangs together; what they decide is which tool to
try in the scene.

orders.title: WO-015 — The soldier scene: twenty units on a 2D canvas behind a renderer seam, a rail of the tools the engine runs with each tool's definition read from the catalog, real-time-strategy selection, flock, arrive and a two-level formation with slot roles, a deterministic seeded clock, before-and-after trials, the first real look, the root route, and the pure scene engine every later scene reuses
orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens the app and lands
on `/scene`: twenty units idling on a dark field that fills the page below
the shell's header, each labelled with a lifecycle role and coloured by it;
a narrow rail on the right lists the tools the engine runs, grouped by what
they do (move: seek, arrive, wander; group: separation, cohesion, velocity
matching, flock; avoid: priority steering; form: wedge, line, column, with
two-level and fixed formation and slot roles), each name in its work's
colour; an instrument strip along the bottom shows cohesion radius,
collisions, heading variance, time to objective and stalled units at their
idle values beside the seed and the transport. They drag a marquee round
twelve units (or click, shift-click, double-click a squad, Escape to clear,
or Tab and Space through the text layer below the field). They choose Flock
in the rail and the inspector shows the catalog's definition of flocking in
a readable measure, its five faces as a sentence, its three weights as
sliders with defaults, and ghost arrows on the selected units showing the
first frame's accelerations. They apply: the twelve pull together and move
as a group, the cohesion radius falls, collisions stay at zero, and a
sparkline under each figure shows the change. They click the field to set an
objective and apply Arrive: the group slows and stops inside the target
radius. They select eight more and apply Formation: wedge; the units sort
themselves into slots, the hardest to place first, while the slot table in
the inspector fills from the cost table. They open Compare and see the
branch before the equip as a ghost under the branch after, two series per
metric, with the first divergence frame marked; they keep the trial. They
save the composition, reload, and find it. Under reduced motion the field is
still until they press Step or Play; the same seed and the same steps
reproduce the same frames; nothing leaves the browser. A tool opened from
the catalog's "runs in the soldier scene" link arrives chosen in the rail.
What the operator learns is what each movement idea does to a group when
they can see it; what they decide is which ideas to keep and which to try
on the agents next.

goalReview.goalStandard:
## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,

The toolbox catalog and the toy shelf, which the vision ties to the scene, live under Tools, the side utilities. The convention documents will encode this ambiguity for every later sub-app to follow.
